transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Lately, my mind has been feeling very foggy, and I just can’t seem to focus or make decisions the way I used to. It’s gotten to the point where it's really affecting my day-to-day life, so I decided it was time to get some help.
Have you experienced these feelings of fogginess and difficulty focusing before in your life, or is this the first time you have felt this way?

Looking back, these big swings from feeling overly revved up to months of feeling foggy and drained have actually been coming and going for several years. However, this current low stretch really took hold after my sister’s heart problems worsened.
During those times when you felt 'overly revved up,' did you find that you needed much less sleep than usual, felt unusually energetic, or found yourself taking on many new projects or risks?

Yes, during those times I felt incredibly wired and energetic, often staying up half the night reorganizing my sister's closets or updating my website without feeling tired at all. I would pile on way too many client projects and tasks all at once because I felt completely unstoppable and couldn't sit still.
During those 'revved up' periods, did your behavior become so extreme that it caused significant problems at work or in your relationships, or did you require hospitalization to keep you safe?

No, it never got to the point of needing hospitalization, and it didn't cause major problems at the time—I actually felt highly productive, energized, and completely in my flow, though I did occasionally snap at people if they slowed me down. The real problems, like missing bill payments and having to turn down work, only started when I crashed into this current foggy, low phase.

During your current low phase, have you experienced a persistent loss of interest or pleasure in almost all of your usual activities, or do you find you can still enjoy things if the circumstances are right?

Yes, I've completely lost interest in the things I used to love. I used to get so much joy out of sketching store layouts or throwing pottery for my shop, but lately, I look at the clay and feel absolutely nothing. I usually just end up turning off the lights and going back to bed or watching TV.
During these low periods, have you ever felt that life is not worth living or had any thoughts of harming yourself?

Yes, on the drives back from my sister's, I sometimes catch myself thinking it might be easier for everyone if I just didn't wake up one morning. I haven't made any plans to hurt myself, but those kinds of thoughts have been popping up and lingering more often lately.

During this current period, have you experienced any physical slowing, significant changes in your appetite or weight, or a sense of worthlessness that makes it difficult for you to function for most of the day?

Yes, I feel physically slowed down, like I'm moving through molasses just walking to my sister's door, and I'll sit staring at my computer for ages before I can type. I also constantly beat myself up with guilt, feeling worthless and like I'm letting everyone down, though I haven't really noticed any changes in my appetite or weight.
During this current period, have these feelings of worthlessness and lack of energy been so severe that you have been unable to perform your work or household tasks for most of the day?

Yes, they have severely impacted my daily life. Over the last couple of months, I’ve had to turn down new consulting projects, postpone work for longtime clients, and rely heavily on my husband to handle basic tasks like paying bills because I’m just too exhausted to keep up.
Has this current period of feeling worthless, exhausted, and unable to function lasted for at least two consecutive weeks?

Yes, it's been much longer than two weeks; this low period has actually been dragging on for about six months now. It started just a few weeks after I began making those regular weekend trips to help my sister, and I've felt this exhausted ever since.
